title: People of the Living God
description: People of the Living God in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 660 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Joined to God's People”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Peo-ple of the liv-ing God, I have sought the world a-round, Paths of sin and sor-row trod, Peace and com-fort no-where found.

lines: I have sought the world around,
Paths of sin and sorrow trod,
Now to you my spirit turns, —
Like the cloud, the wind, the wave;
Where you dwell shall be my home,
Where you die shall be my grave.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
